review.summary:
At risk. Local checks: 23 tests passed; link checker reports bad 0. External claims were not verified offline.
Checkpoint recovery can duplicate side effects.
The provenance guard can accept poisoned archive numbers.
The example grader crashes on ordinary inputs.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches and worked answers
findings.title: A checkpointed done set does not guarantee safe replay
findings.claim: The answer claims that a done set makes replay safe wherever the checkpoint sits. A crash after the external action but before saving its completion loses the done entry and repeats the action. Saving after tool results also cannot prevent crashes inside that unsaved interval.
findings.evidence: A local reproduction executed a ticket write, updated the in-memory done set, simulated a crash by restoring the previous checkpoint, and resumed with the same call id. It created two tickets. The exercise explicitly kills the process inside the executor, before the turn-boundary save. The unconditional guarantee repeats in the Week 3 self-quiz answer and glossary.md's Done set entry.
findings.proposed_change: Explain the crash window and require destination-side idempotency using a durably preserved operation id, or an atomic transaction covering the effect and its completion record. Qualify the byte-identical-resume claim and update the repeated answers and glossary. Verify crashes before execution, after the effect but before saving, and after saving; each must create at most one ticket.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: contradictions between lessons and worked answers
findings.title: Tool-result membership does not establish trusted provenance
findings.claim: The stated provenance rule accepts any number returned by a tool, but archive_read_doc is itself a tool that returns the forged number. Consequently, the worked answer's claim that no tool returned 38 contradicts the extractor's described output. Scalar membership also accepts a matching number from an unrelated metric, site or window.
findings.evidence: Line 939 routes archive_read_doc through the extractor; line 951 explicitly says that extractor passes through 38. Lesson 6.3 implements provenance as t[0].value in trial.tool_values. With archive value 38 and trusted weather value 4, the membership check accepts 38.
findings.proposed_change: Require evidence references carrying tool-call id, trusted origin, site, window, metric and units. Exclude archive extraction and other untrusted-derived values from authoritative measurements. Update the guard, grader, worked answers and glossary. Verify that archive-only 38 and matching numbers from unrelated measurements fail while the trusted weather measurement passes.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches and worked answers
findings.title: The grader crashes on missing tickets and judge verdicts
findings.claim: The grader records the ticket-count check but does not branch before indexing the first ticket. It also sums the judge's pass/fail/unknown verdict together with boolean gates. These ordinary outcomes raise exceptions instead of producing grades.
findings.evidence: Executing the supplied function with an empty should-file sink raises IndexError at t[0]. With one correct ticket and judge returning 'pass', it raises TypeError at sum(g.values()). The surrounding explanation says the judge returns pass/fail/unknown and is reported separately.
findings.proposed_change: Handle an invalid ticket count before dereferencing a ticket. Compute partial credit from the boolean code gates, and store the judge verdict separately with an explicit unknown policy. Verify zero, one and multiple tickets and all three judge verdicts.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches and worked answers
findings.title: The integrative loop treats truncated responses as stalls
findings.claim: Every non-refusal stop other than tool_use receives a submission nudge. This includes max_tokens with a partial tool-use block, which remains in the transcript without a corresponding result. The next request violates the tool-message invariant taught earlier instead of retrying the truncated response.
findings.evidence: Running the actual function with a mocked max_tokens response containing a partial tool request produced the next request as: user task, assistant partial tool_use, user 'Not submitted yet'. No matching tool_result existed. Lesson 2.5 explicitly requires retrying a truncated tool call with a larger output cap.
findings.proposed_change: Handle truncation and other exceptional stop reasons explicitly before retaining a response for continuation. Retry a truncated tool request from the preceding consistent transcript with a larger cap; reserve the submission nudge for a genuine end_turn. Verify the next request after a simulated truncated tool call has no dangling tool request.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches do what the text says
findings.title: Reassigning the plan does not change the active iterator
findings.claim: The for loop obtains its pending-step iterator once. Reassigning plan to the replanner's new object does not change that iterator, so removed steps still run and inserted steps are skipped.
findings.evidence: A local reproduction replaced the plan after weather with a pipeline_status step. Execution still followed metrics, weather, curtailment, compare; pipeline_status never ran. This contradicts the next paragraph's example of dropping curtailment/comparison and inserting a pipeline check.
findings.proposed_change: Use a bounded loop that selects the next pending step from the current plan after every replanning response. Verify that a weather outage causes pipeline_status to run next and that removed steps never execute.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: arithmetic and worked answers
findings.title: The monitoring rule misses declining confirmation rates
findings.claim: The answer alerts only when the signed z-score exceeds positive 3, then claims that falling confirmation rates trigger it. Under the supplied formula, the planted decline produces a negative score and does not trigger that rule.
findings.evidence: For the answer's baseline 0.85, observed rate 0.60 and n=30, (0.60-0.85)/sqrt(0.85*0.15/30) equals -3.8348, not positive 3.8. The approval-confirmation gap is mentioned but its alert statistic is not defined.
findings.proposed_change: Specify the adverse direction for each metric: upper-tail alerts for failures and lower-tail alerts for confirmation or cache-hit rates. Alternatively define an explicit gap statistic. Verify both the planted confirmation decline and an equally large improvement, with only the adverse change triggering a degradation alert.

findings.title: Reviewer override rate is not true negative rate
findings.claim: The text equates the share of flagged tickets that reviewers approve with TNR. These metrics condition on different populations, so one cannot establish the other or justify a judge's release threshold.
findings.evidence: Lesson 5.3's review defines override rate as approved flagged tickets divided by all flagged tickets. Lesson 6.3 defines TNR as judge-failed human failures divided by all human failures. With TP=80, FN=20, TN=5 and FP=5, override rate is 20/25=0.80 while TNR is 5/10=0.50.
findings.proposed_change: Keep override rate as a useful operational signal, but remove the equivalence. Calculate TNR from human-labelled failures, including failures the judge did not flag. Add a small confusion-matrix example showing both denominators.

findings.title: The diagnosis example cannot clear T1 with the stated keep setting
findings.claim: The example attributes the failure to clearing the first tool result, but only three tool calls precede T4. The linked configuration keeps the last three tool uses, so crossing the token threshold alone cannot remove T1.
findings.evidence: The table lists only read_memory, metrics_get_site and weather_get_history before T4. Lesson 3.2 specifies keep 3 in the exercise and a default keep of 3; its example code keeps 4. None of these settings permits the claimed T1 removal in this trace.
findings.proposed_change: State a configuration that actually clears T1, such as keep 2, or extend the trace with enough intervening calls. Show which result the applied-edits record removed before claiming the diagnosis is confirmed.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: contradictions affecting release and monitoring decisions
findings.title: The harness hash omits behavior-changing implementation
findings.claim: Hashing only prompt text, tool definitions and optionally the skill listing cannot identify every harness version. Executor, loop, guardrail and skill-body changes can alter outcomes while retaining the same hash, undermining later comparisons and diagnosis.
findings.evidence: Lesson 5.5 defines this restricted hash; lesson 6.5 says every harness change gets a new hash. Lesson 7.5's executor-retry fix can leave all hashed text unchanged, while lesson 7.4 uses an unchanged hash to point away from code and toward vendor degradation.
findings.proposed_change: Define a harness version from a reproducible code artifact or commit plus prompt/tool/skill contents and behavior-changing configuration. Keep infrastructure metadata separately as already required. Verify that changing an executor retry policy or skill body changes the version even when descriptions stay identical.
